report.objective: Implement GOV.ORCH.12: a movement whose engineer raised a RELAY_QUESTION and exited cleanly becomes resumable once the Product Owner answers on the relay. Today such a record is terminal, so answering costs a fresh dispatch and a full baseline re-run (observed on three movements). The change is confined to scripts/orchestrator.py's pure decision layer plus its recovery note, and its tests.

requirements: English, per AGENTS.md engineering-output language law.
Every new function and test names the clause it implements (GOV.ORCH.12 RQ-n).
Do NOT run the full Python test suite; run only the three orchestrator test files named in test_baseline plus the privacy gate.
The safety must live in ONE pure predicate that decide_start and its caller both read, exactly as _is_resumable_budget_failure does -- never a second re-derivation.
If a clause of GOV.ORCH.12 and this packet disagree, raise a RELAY_QUESTION and STOP.
No emoji, no tool-identifying footer, no external URL in commits, the PR or code comments.
Commit early and often. The SESSION_CLOSE names the predicate, the record field added, the decide_start branch, the note change, and the test counts before and after.

Treating any relay entry as an answer regardless of its author role.
Touching the budget branch's refusal semantics.

Read the entries' role field to tell engineer from po; if an entry has no role, treat it as not an answer.

RQ-3: the record carries the index (or timestamp) of the answer the last resume consumed -- add one field to the process record (for example last_resumed_answer_index) written where the resume is recorded; a resume is allowed only when a qualifying answer exists strictly after that mark. With no newer answer, decide_start returns a refusal whose reason names that the relay has no Product Owner answer newer than the last resume.

entries.subject: RQ-2 relay entry role field conflict
entries.text: Focused CLI test shows local_relay append entries are not recognized through the required role field, so the GOV.ORCH.12 predicate default-closes every PO answer. RQ-2 requires role and says missing role is not an answer, while this movement may not change local_relay. Please authorize the exact compatible entry identity field or a scoped contract correction.

entries.subject: RQ-2 field names corrected: GOV.ORCH.12-A
entries.text: Correct, and thank you for stopping instead of substituting. The defect is the Product Owner's: RQ-2 named a per-entry 'role' field and a per-entry 'next_actor'; scripts/local_relay.py writes neither. The correction is now FROZEN on main as docs/design/GOV_ORCH_12A_THE_RELAY_FIELDS_RQ2_ACTUALLY_READS.md -- read it and implement RQ-2 from it: authorship is the entry's 'actor' field (values po and engineer; no actor means not an answer), ordering is the entry's 'seq' field (never the list position), and an answer is a po-authored entry with marker RELAY_DECISION, RELAY_CORRECTION or RELAY_NOTE whose seq is greater than the stopping RELAY_QUESTION's seq, together with the relay's top-level next_actor equal to 'engineer'. Everything else in RQ-2 stands unchanged: phase failed, exit_code 0, failure_reasons exactly {relay_not_closed}, default-closed. Nothing else in the packet changes; local_relay.py stays untouched.

entries.subject: GOV.ORCH.12 RQ-2 answer-position conflict
entries.text: WORKER.md permits a qualifying Product Owner answer anywhere after the engineer RELAY_QUESTION (using the last answer index), while approved_task.json's FROZEN-contract summary requires the relay entries to end in the Product Owner answer. Which condition governs when entries are appended after the answer?

entries.subject: GOV.ORCH.12-A RQ-2c governs; 'entries end with' is superseded prose
entries.text: Good catch again, and it is the Product Owner's prose defect, not a real conflict. GOV.ORCH.12-A is the correcting amendment to RQ-2 and it restates the whole condition; where its RQ-2c and RQ-2's older sentence differ, RQ-2c governs. Concretely, the condition is NOT positional: an answer qualifies when (a) it is a po-authored entry with marker RELAY_DECISION, RELAY_CORRECTION or RELAY_NOTE, (b) its seq is greater than the seq of the engineer RELAY_QUESTION that stopped the run, and (c) the relay's top-level next_actor equals 'engineer' at the moment the decision is taken. Entries appended after the answer do not disqualify it; the top-level next_actor is what carries whose turn it is, and it is the only turn signal the decision reads. If next_actor has flipped back to 'po' (someone asked something new), that is not resumable and the refusal names it. Implement exactly this; no further authorization is needed on this point, and this note is itself an example of the shape you are matching. Nothing else in the packet changes.
